texts.content:
These amalgams follow no fixed patterns, their form, mobility,
and aggression vary depending on the nature of the remains,
making them volatile threats that defy anticipation.
Some develop multiple limbs, others crawl as pulsating
heaps, and some extend themselves as living nets.
Their emergence signals that the plague, even in apparent
defeat, continues to seek new ways to persist and adapt,
reclaiming whatever fragments it can to fuel its evolution.

These entities are not infected in the conventional sense,
but rather aberrant by products of the eradication process.
They tend to manifest during intense combat scenarios,
especially when infected remains are not incinerated swiftly.
Residual biomass (vascular tissue, cartilage, bone fragments,
and active larvae) spontaneously fuses into chaotic
amalgams: masses composed of incompatible parts that
nonetheless operate with unpredictable lethality.
